rows.description: The wrongdoer is a friend who helped me settle in, and I feel torn. Wise: loyalty to a person and loyalty to truth can clash; give him a chance to correct it, but do not stay silent forever. Harmful: excuses.

rows.description: I noticed something wrong earlier and said nothing, and now it is bigger. Wise: speak up now, acknowledge the delay, and let the facts lead. Harmful: staying silent because I already stayed silent.

rows.description: I reported and nothing happened, and I feel cynical about all systems. Wise: try another channel, connect with groups that know the process, and keep some faith in change. Harmful: deciding nobody can be trusted.

rows.description: A few colleagues quietly thank me for speaking up. It gives me courage. Wise: value the support, but do not expect them to stand publicly; protect them and myself. Harmful: making them feel guilty for their silence.

rows.description: In a new city or country I fear making mistakes with language, food and rules. Wise: ask, watch, be patient with a learning curve, and find a small community. Harmful: staying only in a bubble that never lets me learn.

rows.description: People are polite but never invite me in, and my accent makes me feel like an outsider. Wise: keep showing up in clubs, classes and small talk; belonging is built slowly. Harmful: assuming all locals dislike me.

rows.description: I adapt to new ways and feel I am betraying my parents' culture. Wise: identity can hold both; keep what I value and adopt what suits me, and explain it to family. Harmful: hiding one half to please the other.

rows.description: I miss home food, language and family and cry in secret. Wise: schedule calls, cook familiar meals, find fellow migrants, and know that it eases with time. Harmful: isolating or judging myself for missing home.
